newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Marines evacuate over 1,000 from Sierra Leone.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Marines evacuate over 1,000 from Sierra Leone.

text.p: U.S. helicopters staged a third evacuation of foreigners from Sierra Leone on Tuesday, ferrying more than 1,000 people including about 20 Americans to a U.S. warship, the Defence Department said.
"There have been no casualties. It has been a well-run operation. They are all out, off the beach now," Defence Secretary William Cohen told reporters after Marines completed the operation.

It was the third round of evacuations since Friday from the capital Freetown to the USS Kearsarge, which was sent to the West African country's Atlantic coast amid fears of widespread violence after the Army staged a coup. Tuesday's evacuation brought to nearly 2,500 the total number of persons including some 430 Americans removed since Friday.

"The final number (on Tuesday) is 1,217 and all of the Marines are off the beach," Marine Corps Lt. Gen. James Jones, Cohen's senior military aide, said. Cohen spoke briefly with reporters after a picture session with visiting Slovenian Defence Minister Tit Turnsek.

Defence officials said Tuesday's evacuees were removed from a beachfront near a restaurant. All U.S. evacuees in last week's operation were taken from Freetown's Mammy Yoko Hotel but that had become too dangerous as an evacuation point.
"We've heard reports of fires and there's been fighting in the area," Pentagon spokeswoman Lt. Col. Nancy Burt said.
CH-53 "Sea Stallion" helicopters, which can carry up to 55 passengers, and CH-46 "Sea Knight" helicopters, capable of carrying 22 passengers, have been used in the evacuations.

Washington is encouraging an end to violence and the restoration of democracy in the country after a military coup nine days ago threw out democratically elected President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah. But it has been equivocal about whether it supports military efforts by Nigeria, which with other West African states has hundreds of troops in the country, to overturn the coup and restore Kabbah.
